findings.text: panel_engines and its helpers _engine_entry (:778) and _lane_document (:866) are 95 new production lines with no test. Nothing outside live_panel.py references panel_engines, tests/test_live_panel.py is declared in the fence and was left untouched, and replacing the function body with "return []" leaves all 94 tests green, so the join that produces every per-engine entry is unguarded.

the pool/live join matches on host alone although both sides carry the served model (the live entry's served_name, the pool entry's model_id) and the live entry carries job_id, so two serves on one host are paired by list order. Demonstrated against the reviewed head with pool engines :18810 (m-a, available 64) and :18812 (m-b, available 5) and the live entries given in the other order: the entry returned for :18810 carries m-b's live figures (running 12.0) beside m-a's gate (available 64). During a restart overlap — two same-model serves on one host in one pool — each engine's availability and queue are published beside the other engine's throughput and running count.

the live path reads one lane document, and lane.py:1322 compose_pool_document adds an engines array only to a pool document spanning more than one engine while router.py:2858 writes one pool document per model into lanes/<model>.json; the engines of a second model therefore never reach document["engines"], although the committed golden and the fragment at watch-shows-several-engines.html:27 show "3 servers - 3 engines - 2 models", a state only the hand-built fixture produces. The decided single-pool deployment (the B300 serving the H200 model) is spanned and works.

baseline_suite claims 90 passed at the base revision, but no base-revision run appears in the reviewed stream; the only full-suite run before the new tests were added (stream 17:38) reports 84 passed with the feature code already edited, and an independent base arm at 447bf316 run by this review in a scratch tree reports "84 passed in 0.71s" EXIT=0. added_failure_count is 0 under either count because both arms are green, but the recorded base figure is wrong and has no log behind it.

the multi-engine branch of engine_refusal and the explicit selection path it gates (main at llm_watch.py:1180 passing engine= into render_text, and selected_engine at :547) have no test; the refusal tests predate the change, no added test passes --engine, an earlier draft test for it was deleted during the run, and setting main's engine= argument back to None leaves all 94 tests green.

the fragment names "outcomes.engines/outcomes.by_engine", but lane_callers.py publishes only by_engine under outcomes (lane_callers.py:816ff), so a reader who looks for outcomes.engines finds no such key.
